bpn.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
bpn.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

bpn.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
bpn.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

bpn.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
bpn.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

mhp.context: Pressure pipe carrying water from a reservoir or headpond down to a turbine in a micro-hydro system. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Penstock' is a specialized term with no exact one-word equivalent in many languages. Use the established civil/hydro engineering phrase for 'pressure conduit' or 'force main to turbine'. Czech: 'tlakovod' (pressure main) is preferred over the generic 'přiváděcí potrubí' (supply pipe). Serbian: 'напорни цевовод' is the standard hydraulic engineering term. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files. 2026-07-13 Task 103 follow-up: am/bn/ru values below were themselves stale phonetic transliterations of the English word (same defect class as the earlier 'riprap' audit) — corrected to compositional 'pressure pipe' phrases matching the shipped, agent-fixed lang files. When English 'penstock' itself reads as jargon, pair the primary term with a plain '(supply pipe)' gloss in the UI rather than leaving it unglossed — see mhp_diameter tooltip pattern. Task 130 (2026-07-21): the (supply pipe) gloss was applied to mhp_diameter in the 15 languages that lacked the tooltip; each language reused its existing penstock term (no term changes, wrapper+gloss only).

mhp.context: Total elevation difference between the headpond water surface and the turbine — before subtracting penstock losses. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Gross' means total/before-deduction. Pair with 'net head' for clarity. Use the hydro-power standard term.

mhp.context: Effective head available at the turbine after subtracting penstock friction and minor losses from gross head. H_net = H_gross - h_L.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Net' means after-deduction. Pair with 'gross head'. Use the hydro-power standard term. WMO No. 385 entry 111 ('available head') gives the Russian term 'полезный напор' (useful head) / syn. 'располагаемый напор' — these overlap with net head in Russian hydro engineering practice.

mhp.context: Overall efficiency of a micro-hydro power plant — product of turbine, generator, and transmission efficiencies. Dimensionless, 0–1. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Plant' here means the power plant/installation, not a living plant. Use the energy/electrical engineering term for overall system efficiency. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files.

mhp.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred. Standardized to 'افت هد' suite-wide for fa and fixed dw_/hw_ labels in lib/lang.ec.fa.php to match. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 sw wave-3 sprint): glossary sw value was 'upotevu wa shinikizo' (= pressure loss), the same pressure-loss-sense defect class as the ro/tr/id/fa fixes above. But lib/lang.ec.sw.php's own dw_main_desc/dw_main_menu/dw_main_title/mphl_main_desc/mphl_main_menu/mphl_main_title (and mpf_velocity_head, ws_headWaterHeight, or_head, mhp_gross_head elsewhere in the file) all already establish 'Kichwa' (head) as the suite's real Swahili word for hydraulic head, not 'shinikizo' (pressure). Standardized the glossary to 'upotevu wa kichwa' to match the file's own established, correct usage instead of the stale pressure-sense glossary value. Standardized the glossary to 'د سر ضیاع' to match the file's actual established usage, same defect class as the sw fix above. mhp.context: A hydropower configuration that uses natural river flow without a dam or significant storage reservoir. Power output varies with seasonal river flow. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: Use the established energy/hydropower sector term. 'Run' means natural river current — do not translate as jogging or running. WMO No. 385 entry 1263 gives the full facility names: Spanish 'central hidroeléctrica de pasada', French 'usine hydroélectrique au fil de l'eau', Russian 'русловая гидроэлектростанция' — these are the authoritative terms for the power plant noun. The abbreviated forms 'filo de agua' (es), 'au fil de l'eau' (fr), and 'русловая ГЭС' (ru) are standard in engineering use. German: 'Laufwasserkraftwerk'. Chinese: '径流式水电'. Task 98 audit (2026-07-13): 'micro-hydro' (the companion term this concept pairs with in mhp_ keys) had been left completely untranslated/transliterated in 4 languages, not just run-of-river — sw and km kept the raw Latin 'Micro-Hydro' embedded in otherwise-native sentences; km and ps also left 'Run-of-River' in an English parenthetical even where the surrounding sentence already translated the concept; ps separately phonetically transliterated 'مایکرو هایدرو' as its own word throughout (same defect, different script). All 4 fixed: sw → 'Umeme Mdogo wa Maji' (small electricity of water), km → 'ថាមពលវារីអគ្គិសនីខ្នាតតូច' (small-scale hydroelectric power, reusing km's own native hydro vocabulary), ps → 'کوچنی آبي ځواک' (small water-power, real Pashto not transliteration) with the redundant English '(Run-of-River)' parenthetical dropped in both km and ps since their own sentences already conveyed it. ar ('الطاقة الكهرومائية الصغيرة') and zh ('微型水力发电') were already clean and served as the quality reference for the fixes.
mhp.preferred_translation: pembangkit listrik tenaga air aliran langsung

mhp.context: The intake structure at the upstream end of a penstock or canal, where water is diverted from the river or reservoir into the conveyance system. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator (penstock diameter and length descriptions).
mhp.translation_notes: Use the civil/irrigation engineering term for a water intake or diversion structure. Spanish: 'obra de toma'. French: 'ouvrage de prise d'eau'. Russian: 'водозаборное сооружение'. German: 'Einlaufbauwerk'. In many languages, 'intake structure' is preferred over a literal translation of 'headworks'.

mhp.context: Energy loss at pipe junctions, bends, fittings, and entrance — a local (point) loss as opposed to distributed friction loss along the pipe. h_m = k_m × v²/(2g). Appears in Manning Pipe Head Loss and Micro-Hydro Power calculators.
mhp.translation_notes: CANONICAL ENGLISH (label-normalization decision, item 90, 2026-07-07): the suite-wide English label for this concept is "Minor (local) loss" — 'junction loss' (formerly mphl_) and 'minor loss' (mhp_/ip_) are merged into it; see the 'minor loss' entry for the canonical treatment. The term 'minor' is conventional but misleading — do not imply these losses are always small; the parenthetical '(local)' carries the true sense. Use the hydraulic engineering term for local/point losses at fittings. French: 'perte singulière'. Spanish: 'pérdida local' or 'pérdida por accesorio'. Russian: 'местные потери'. Chinese: '局部水头损失'. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): de mphl_total_junction_k_tip aligned to örtlich/'(local)' label wording; hi/id/ur had the 'minor (local)' word order reversed against their own labels and were corrected.

mhp.context: Local head loss at fittings/valves/couplers (coefficient k_m). Canonical merged concept for the former 'junction loss' (mphl_) and 'minor loss' (mhp_/ip_). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure.
mhp.translation_notes: CANONICAL ENGLISH LABEL: "Minor (local) loss" (label-normalization decision, item 90, 2026-07-07). 'Minor ⇄ local' — a local/point loss at fittings, NOT a "smaller" loss; the '(local)' parenthetical fixes the mistranslation trap. Symbol h_m, coefficient k_m (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per the same decision). am ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 am re-translation): 'ጥቃቅን (አካባቢያዊ) ኪሳራ' (tiqaqin (akababiyawi) kisara) mirrors the English structure word-for-word — 'ጥቃቅን' (minor/small) followed by the parenthetical '(አካባቢያዊ)' (local, i.e. of a specific place/area) — so the same mistranslation-blocking device English uses (the '(local)' qualifier preventing a 'smaller loss' misreading) is preserved in Amharic rather than silently dropped. Replaces the prior am file's 'የማያያዣ ኪሳራ' (connector/joint loss), which named the physical fitting rather than the local/point-loss concept. km ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 km re-translation): 'ការបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋាន' (local-basis loss) reuses មូលដ្ឋាន ('local', already established suite-wide for this exact merged concept in ip_km's tooltip 'មេគុណបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋានសរុប' = 'total local-loss coefficient'), so category-3 now converges on the same word ip_ already uses rather than coining a second competing term. Deliberately avoids 'តូច' (small), sidestepping the minor⇄smaller mistranslation trap the English '(local)' parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the km file's prior mphl_junction_loss value 'ការបាត់បង់ junction' (untranslated English word left in place). ps ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 ps wave-3 re-translation): 'ځایی ضیاع' (local loss) uses ځایی (local/positional) + the established ps loss word ضیاع, following the majority pattern already set by ar/fa/es/fr/hr/id/it/ro/ru/sr/tr/uk/ur/zh — all of which render this concept as 'local loss' alone rather than translating 'minor' literally, since the '(local)' qualifier is the operative disambiguator, not 'minor'. Deliberately avoids a word for 'small/minor' (e.g. کوچنی) to sidestep the same minor⇄smaller trap the English parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the prior ps file's 'د جنکشن ضیاع' (junction loss — the pre-consolidation, pre-item-90 term) and fixes its symbol from capital H_m to lowercase h_m. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): de 'Minderverlust' (=lesser/reduced loss — the exact 'smaller loss' mistranslation the item-90 convention blocks) corrected to 'Örtlicher (Einzel-)Verlust' matching the labels.

mtc.context: Cross-sectional flow area divided by wetted perimeter. Appears in Manning calculators.
mtc.translation_notes: Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used the Latin loanword 'hidraulički radijus' — this form is widely used in South Slavic engineering practice and may be more recognizable to field practitioners than the native Slavic equivalents 'полупречник' (sr) / 'polumjer' (hr). Both are correct; native Slavic engineers may encounter both forms. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 sw wave-3 sprint): previous sw value 'radius ya maji' (literally 'radius of water', English loanword 'radius' + 'of water') named the substance rather than the hydraulic-geometry property, and did not read as an engineering term. Changed to 'radiasi ya kihaidroliki' (radius + 'hydraulic', adjectival ki- form), matching the '[radius] + hydraulic' construction used by fr/de/it/es/ro/tr (rayon hydraulique / hydraulischer Radius / raggio idraulico / radio hidráulico / raza hidraulică / hidrolik yarıçap). Used in lib/lang.ec.sw.php's mpf_hydraulic_radius.

mtc.context: Length of the channel or pipe boundary in contact with flowing water. Appears in Manning calculators.
mtc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 1682 confirms: es = 'perímetro mojado', fr = 'périmètre mouillé'. Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. 'Wetted' here means 'in contact with water', not 'soaked'. Pre-2026 sr human used 'okvašeni obim' (obim = natural South Slavic word for perimeter/circumference); current uses 'квашени периметар' (периметар = Greek-derived loanword). Both are correct; 'obim/opseg' is more natural in informal Serbian/Croatian field use. Task 109 stages 4 & 5 (2026-07-19): bg wrong-word 'навлажнен' (moistened) corrected to 'омокрен' in mpf_wetted_perimeter (stage 4) and cs_notes_3_def (stage 5); km គ្រែទឹក (water bed) also confirmed corrected to glossary បរិវេណសើម (stage 4).

mtc.context: Manning's n — empirical roughness coefficient used in the Manning formula for open-channel and pipe flow.
mtc.translation_notes: Always include 'Manning' as a proper noun. The coefficient itself (n) needs no translation — only the label does. Do not translate as generic 'roughness coefficient' without 'Manning'. TYPO FIX 2026-07-09 (category-3 wave-1 sprint): ru/uk transliterations were single-н 'Манинга'/'Манінга', flagged by the ru wave-1 agent as inconsistent with the established double-н transliteration ('Маннинга'/'Маннінга') used 11+ times elsewhere in both lang files (predates this sprint). Corrected to double-н for consistency. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): am 3-way 'roughness' spelling drift standardized to file-dominant ሻካሪነት (was ሻካርነት); it confirmed on scabrezza and sw on usuguo (both already glossary-correct). [2026-07-24] he corrected: was transliterated 'מנינג'; shipped lang.ec.he.php uses Latin 'Manning' throughout (mi_/mpf_/mphl_ menus), so glossary now matches file practice.

mtc.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
mtc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

rc.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
rc.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

rc.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
rc.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

rc.context: Angular rock placed to resist erosion on channel beds and banks. Appears in Manning Trapezoidal Channel and Rock Chute calculators.
rc.translation_notes: No direct single-word equivalent in most languages. Use the established local engineering term — this varies significantly by country. In Spanish, 'enrocado' (general) or 'escollera' (bank protection) are both used; lead with 'enrocado'. Bulgarian terms verified/corrected by a native Bulgarian engineer, 2026-07 (dev/Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md). bg: 'каменна облицовка' (stone lining), not 'каменна наброска'. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files. Task 97 (2026-07-13): tr's rock-chute (rc_) translation agent had actually diverged from this glossary value, using 'parça taşı' (rock fragment/piece) in 4 places instead of 'taş dolgu'; no native Turkish reviewer was available, so resolved by an AI (Opus) judgment call reasoning from suite convention — 'taş dolgu' ('stone fill', the established DSİ/TS term, cf. 'taş dolgu baraj' = rockfill dam) is correct for both the bulk-material and D50 particle-sizing senses, matching how es/fr/pt/ru all keep one bulk-material word rather than switching to a fragment/particle term for sizing contexts. Lang file corrected to 'taş dolgu' throughout; treat as our best-effort resolution, not pending native review (see CLAUDE.md 'Native review is real only when feedback actually lands'). Task 98 riprap audit (2026-07-13): found 6 of 26 languages (am, bn, he, hi, id, ur) had phonetically TRANSLITERATED the English word 'riprap' as a borrowed loanword instead of translating the concept — a real translation-quality defect, not a stylistic choice, concentrated in this specific bare/short-label term. English source renamed 'riprap' → 'rock lining' (see CLAUDE.md 'Write English source strings in Simple English') specifically because a transparent two-word English compound is much less likely to be transliterated than an opaque-looking jargon word; all 6 languages' rc_/mtc_ occurrences were corrected to real native terms in the same pass (each reusing that language's own already-successful translation pattern found elsewhere in its file). zh was separately found to use three inconsistent terms (块石/护坡/抛石) for this concept across different rc_ keys — not a transliteration issue, but the same 'pick one term and use it everywhere' defect — resolved by standardizing on 护坡 (slope protection/lining), which best matches the 'lining' sense and was already the plurality incumbent. The other 19 languages already had good native terms and needed no change — the concept translated fine, only the English word choice invited transliteration risk in weaker-resourced languages. Task 109 stage 2 (2026-07-19): ar/km/my/sw confirmed on real translated words — the phonetic-transliteration failure class (same as the 2026-07-13 rc_ audit) was checked and corrected where present.

rc.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
rc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

rc.context: A steep rock-lined drop structure (also called a 'rock ramp') that conveys water rapidly down a slope in irrigation, drainage, or watershed management. Key concepts for translation: rock-lined, steep gradient, spillway or drop structure — translate the concept, not the English word 'chute'. The rock riprap matrix dissipates energy and resists erosion. Appears in Rock Chute Design (Robinson) and Robinson Rock Chute calculators.
rc.translation_notes: CRITICAL: 'Robinson' is the surname of K.M. Robinson, co-author of Robinson, Rice & Kadavy (1998) — it is a proper noun and must NEVER be translated or modified in any language. Translate only 'Rock Chute'. Concept to translate: 'rock-lined steep channel' or 'rock-lined spillway' — the drop/descent nature must be conveyed; a generic 'rock channel' is insufficient. CRITICAL for French: WMO No. 385 entry 517 establishes that the French word 'chute' means 'fall' (elevation difference) — it cannot name this structure. Use 'coursier en enrochement' (coursier = steep channel structure; enrochement = riprap). Spanish: USDA uses 'bajante de rocado' — 'bajante' (from bajar = to descend) correctly conveys the drop-structure nature; 'de rocado' = rock-lined. Russian: 'каменный быстроток' ('быстроток' = fast-flow/steep channel). Portuguese: changed from 'calha' (generic trough) to 'rampa em enrocamento' (rampa = ramp/slope, enrocamento = riprap) to convey steep character. Serbian: changed from 'жлеб' (gutter/trough) to 'брзоток' (fast-flow structure), consistent with ru/uk pattern. Bengali: changed from borrowed 'চ্যুট' (conveys nothing) to 'পাথর-আবৃত খাড়া নালা' (rock-lined steep channel). Persian: changed from generic 'آبراه سنگی' (stone waterway) to 'آبراه تند سنگچین' (تند = steep/swift, سنگچین = stone-laid/riprap). Pashto: added 'تند' (steep/swift) to original. Khmer: changed 'ចំហ' (open) to 'ជម្រាល' (sloped/inclined). NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: am (ምቀጫ meaning uncertain), my (ထောင် may not clearly convey steep to all readers), de (Steinschütte is standard engineering term but doesn't explicitly say 'steep channel'). Turkish: changed to 'taş düşü' — 'düşü' is the established Turkish hydraulics term for a drop/chute structure (2026-07 audit; previous 'taş eğimli kanal' was descriptive but nonstandard). Spanish: NEEDS HUMAN VERIFICATION — 'bajante de rocado' claims a USDA source but 'rocado' is not standard Spanish ('enrocado' is); verify the USDA document or switch to 'bajante de enrocado'. 2026-07 reconciliation: fr/ro/ru/uk lang files updated to match this entry. NOT reconciled pending human review of the GLOSSARY side: hr 'kameni skluz' (consider 'kameni brzotok', parallel to sr/ru), bg 'каменна бързина' (consider 'каменен бързоток'), de 'Steinschütte' vs shipped 'Steingerinne' (both defensible - pick one). RESOLVED bg: native Bulgarian engineer confirmed 'каменен бързоток' (2026-07); lang file updated. Task 98 (2026-07-13): English source renamed 'Rock Chute' → 'Steep Channel' throughout the rc_ prefix (see CLAUDE.md 'Write English source strings in Simple English') — 'chute' itself is jargon-shaped English that some languages transliterated rather than translated. The earlier Bengali fix noted above only reached the calculator's title-level strings (rc_main_menu/rc_main_desc); a full-file grep found 'চ্যুট' still transliterated in 7 more rc_ body keys (rc_S0, rc_qt, rc_n_chute, rc_pond_ok_tip, rc_pond_warn_tip, rc_notes_2_def, rc_notes_3_def, rc_notes_7_def) — fixed 2026-07-13 to match the title's 'খাড়া নালা'. Hindi and Urdu had the same bare-transliteration defect suite-wide ('चूट'/'چوٹ') despite their titles being fine in some cases — fixed to 'तीव्र ढाल चैनल' (hi) and 'کھڑی نالی' (ur), applied consistently across every rc_ occurrence. Lesson: a healthy title-level translation does not guarantee the same concept was translated (vs. transliterated) in every short body label — check the whole file, not just the title strings, when auditing a jargon term.

rc.context: A steep open channel or drop structure for conveying water rapidly down a slope. Distinct from a gentle-slope irrigation canal. Per ec_lang_intent guidance: translate as 'steep channel' or 'spillway' — not as the word 'chute' borrowed into another language. Appears in Rock Chute Design (Robinson), Manning Trapezoidal Channel, and related drop-structure calculators.
rc.translation_notes: CRITICAL for French: WMO No. 385 entry 517 defines the English word 'fall' (elevation difference) as French 'chute', Spanish 'caída', and Russian 'падение'. The same pattern holds in all three WMO languages: the word for 'fall' (elevation difference) is NOT available for this hydraulic structure. 'Coursier' is the correct French term for the structure. Spanish: 'canal rápido'. Russian: 'быстроток' (the steep channel structure — distinct from 'падение' which means elevation fall). Chinese: '陡槽'. | [2026-07-20] Stage-6 sr audit found the glossary's own value (брзотек) was the stem-drift error; corrected to брзоток, consistent with ru/uk pattern and rc_ identity strings. | [2026-07-20] Stage-6 ps audit aligned to the file's own established identity-string term (تند اوبو لار) over a divergent glossary spelling, for cross-key consistency within category 5.

rc.context: Flow rate per unit width of channel (Q/B), in m²/s or ft²/s. The primary design input for the Robinson rock chute method. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator.
rc.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic engineering term. 'Unit' here means 'per unit channel width' — not related to measurement units. Spanish: 'caudal unitario'. French: 'débit unitaire'. German: 'spezifischer Abfluss'. Russian: 'удельный расход'. Chinese: '单宽流量'. Bulgarian terms verified/corrected by a native Bulgarian engineer, 2026-07 (dev/Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md). bg hydraulics uses 'водно количество' for discharge, not 'дебит'.

rc.context: The particle size at which 50% of the rock is finer by weight. The primary output of the Robinson rock chute method. Also used in Manning Trapezoidal Channel riprap sizing. The symbol D50 is universal — translate only the descriptive label.
rc.translation_notes: D50 (or D₅₀) is a universal engineering symbol — do not translate it. Translate only the label 'median rock size' or 'median particle size'. Most languages express this as 'median diameter'. Do not use 'average' (average ≠ median statistically). Spanish: 'tamaño mediano de roca'. French: 'taille médiane des rochers'. Chinese: '中值粒径'. **2026-07-13 cross-language research pass (item 44):** researched whether 'average/mean'-register wording (found in several languages' initial translations) is a real engineering error or defensible practice-register, using web research into each language's actual geotechnical/sedimentology literature. Confirmed real errors, corrected in both the lang files and this glossary: de ('mittlere'→'mediane'/'medianer', citing German BAW government sedimentology usage), cs ('střední'→'mediánová', citing Charles University hydraulics course), ru ('средний'→'медианный' for mi_d50in; rc_D50 already correct), tr ('orta'→'ortanca', matching the term already correct in rc_D50/rc_notes_1_def), fa ('متوسط'→'میانه', citing Persian percentile-based technical definitions), ur ('اوسط'/'درمیانی'/'درمیانہ'→'وسیط', mirroring Arabic's وسيط/متوسط distinction), sr ('средња'→'медијанска', matching mi_d50in which already used 'Медијана'). Found already correct in the lang files (glossary was simply stale, not the file — see item 42): bg ('медианен размер', confirmed live in mi_d50in/rc_D50/rc_notes_1_def), uk ('медіанний розмір'), hr ('medijalna veličina', an adjective form of medijan/medijana), ro ('dimensiunea mediană'). One language, am (Amharic), was researched and found to have no distinct circulating median-vs-average term at all — even Amharic dictionaries gloss 'median' as 'መካከለኛ' (same word used for 'middle/average') — so 'የድንጋይ መካከለኛ መጠን' was left unchanged; there's no more-correct term available in practice.

rc.context: The spread or uniformity of rock particle sizes. In the Robinson method, gradation is expressed as SD = D84.1/D50. Uniform rock ≈ 1.25; Robinson valid range 1.15–1.47. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator.
rc.translation_notes: Use the geotechnical/hydraulic engineering term for grain size distribution or grading. Do not translate as 'grade' (implies quality). The symbol 'SD' and ratio notation D84.1/D50 are universal. Spanish/Portuguese: 'granulometría'/'granulometria'. French: 'granulométrie'. Russian/Bulgarian/Serbian: 'гранулометрический состав'. Chinese: '级配'. bg: native engineer confirmed 2026-07-06 the standard term for the D84.1/D50 gradation SD label is 'Коефициент на градация' (superseding the earlier 'коефициент на едрозърнестост' proposal and the alternative 'коефициент на разнозърненост'); applied in rc_SD/rc_SD_check. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files.

rc.context: The fraction of the rock layer volume that is void space (air + water). Default 0.45 for angular crushed rock. Determines how much flow passes through the rock mantle versus over the surface. Appears in Rock Chute Design calculator. Distinct from Manning's n (roughness coefficient) — do not confuse the two.
rc.translation_notes: Standard hydraulic/geotechnical term with cognates in most European languages. Always distinguish from Manning 'n' in context — they appear in the same calculator.

rc.context: Dimensionless ratio of a material's density to the density of water (≈2.65 for crushed granite/basalt; Robinson valid range 2.54–2.82). Appears in Rock Chute Design and Manning Trapezoidal Channel. The English source keeps "specific gravity" — the standard English term and the one Robinson's paper uses (rc_ cites it). We deliberately do NOT swap it for "relative density" even though that reads as more modern: per Tom's principle (2026-07-20) we defer to each language's own dominant standard term rather than judging terminology.
rc.translation_notes: [2026-07-20 RESOLUTION — Tom's principle: 'we are not the judges of terminology, culture is.'] Use each language's dominant, culturally-standard term for this dimensionless concept, whatever its literal composition. A weight-flavored STANDARD term is CORRECT, not an error to be reformed toward 'relative density': tr 'özgül ağırlık', he 'משקל סגולי' (standard Hebrew physics-curriculum term), sr 'специфична тежина', ps 'ځانګړی ثقل' are the established local standards and stay. The ONLY hard rule is physical — the value is a dimensionless ratio and never carries units. hr RESOLVED to 'relativna gustoća', the dominant modern Croatian standard (gustoća = density), matching the shipped file; the glossary was the stale side. sw 'uzito maalum' is NOT an auto-defect: if it is the standard Swahili term for the concept used dimensionlessly (parallel to Turkish özgül ağırlık), it is correct — confirm it is the Swahili standard, do not replace it with a coined 'relative density' calque. This supersedes the earlier 'weight-word exception' framing, which wrongly implied 'relative density' was the target to push. [2026-07-21 assessment] Two more glossary values were stale vs. their shipped, internally-consistent files (same class as hr): sr updated 'специфична тежина'→'релативна густина' and it 'peso specifico relativo'→'densità relativa' to match each file's actual standard usage; no lang-file change needed. (Historical: de 'spezifisches Gewicht'→'relative Dichte' and ru 'удельный вес'→'относительная плотность' were corrected in the 2026-07-08 category-1 QA — those were genuine non-standard-in-context values, not the same as a language whose actual standard is weight-flavored.) [2026-07-21 Task 131 tip sprint] 'Density relative to water' definitional tip now ships in all 26 languages on mtc_sgrock/rc_sg. NEW cross-key LABEL drift found (distinct from the glossary-vs-file staleness above): within a single language the two calculators disagree on the SG term — mtc_sgrock uses a weight-flavored label while rc_sg uses a relative-density-flavored one — in pt (Gravidade específica vs Densidade relativa), uk (Питома вага vs Відносна густина), ar (الكثافة النوعية vs الكثافة النسبية), fa (وزن مخصوص نسبی vs چگالی نسبی); sr already noted. Both labels are individually defensible per the cultural-standard rule, but the intra-language inconsistency between the two calculators warrants a future authorized label-consolidation pass. Tips were translated tip-only, labels preserved. [2026-07-21 Task 133 RESOLVED] Authorized label-consolidation pass done: in each affected language mtc_sgrock's divergent weight-flavored label was aligned to rc_sg's relative-density-flavored label (which already matched this entry's dominant-standard translation) — pt→'Densidade relativa da rocha', uk→'Відносна густина каменю', ar→'الكثافة النسبية للصخور', fa→'چگالی نسبی سنگ', sr→'Релативна густина камена'. Both calculators now agree within each language (ar retains a pre-existing singular/plural difference on the rock word only — للصخور vs للصخر — the SG term itself is aligned). Tips untouched (already consistent). Note: this consolidation aligned toward relative-density because rc_sg happened to hold the standard in all 5; it does NOT contradict the cultural-standard rule (a weight-flavored standard like tr/he/sr's own would be equally valid to consolidate toward where it is the dominant term).

rc.context: Water pooling/backing up upstream of the chute inlet; beneficial in the Robinson design context.
rc.translation_notes: Backwater pooling, not flooding: sw "mafuriko" (floods) wrong — use "kutuama kwa maji". Keep one term per language (sw and it files alternate). Task 109 stage 3 (2026-07-19): hi confirmed on ताल — the phonetic transliteration पोंडिंग in wi_pondingHeight was corrected.

rc.context: Flat protective pad of rock/concrete at the chute outlet (hydraulic-structures term). Rock Chute output and sketch label.
rc.translation_notes: Never clothing: it "grembiule" (kitchen apron) wrong — use "platea"; tr "önlük" (bib) wrong. Use the stilling-basin/apron family term: platea/radier/护坦.

rc.context: Upstream water-surface height above the weir crest — a length, not a pressure. Appears in Rock Chute inlet check.
rc.translation_notes: Not a pressure (hr "tlak na pragu" wrong). it: head over a weir = "carico sullo stramazzo" (soglia = sill; "soglio" = throne, wrong). Task 109 stage 3 (2026-07-19): hr ws_headWaterHeight read 'Visina preljeva' (height OF the weir structure) — corrected to 'Preljevna visina' (weir head), the head-vs-structure-height confusion class.
